completion_data.completion_summary: Fixed two deploy-machinery defects: sync.lua's reinject_loaded_extensions() now regenerates CLAUDE.md as a single computed artifact instead of double-appending via retired section markers, and merge.lua's deep_merge gained a matcher-aware, self-normalizing hook-array merge (plus a matching unmerge reversal) that collapses the duplicate claude-stop-notify.sh Stop-hook registration and prevents it recurring. All three verification-bar clauses were demonstrated empirically against a real deploy-headless.sh cycle, with permissions/mcpServers confirmed unaffected and verify-deploy.sh passing 12/12 checks.

memory_candidates.content: In the nvim extension-loader deploy system (lua/neotex/plugins/ai/shared/extensions/merge.lua), Claude Code settings.json hook-event arrays (Stop, PreToolUse, etc.) have a distinct shape from other settings arrays: each item is a {matcher, hooks} table. deep_merge()'s default array-merge compares whole items via vim.deep_equal, which cannot recognize that two differently-shaped {matcher, hooks} blocks sharing the same matcher should be unioned -- this silently produces duplicate hook registrations (e.g. the same script registered twice on Stop) that never self-heal, because merge_settings() only ever adds, never regenerates. The fix pattern: gate a matcher-aware merge behind a strict shape predicate (is_hook_event_array: non-empty array, every item has both a string matcher key and an array-valued hooks key), normalize the target's existing blocks by matcher before merging (idempotent, safe to re-run), and merge incoming blocks by matcher instead of whole-item identity. Track hook-level tracked entries (not just whole-block appends) so unmerge can correctly reverse an entry that got merged into a pre-existing matcher block rather than appended as a new one. Block-grouping normalization should be documented as deliberately NOT reversed by unmerge, since it is semantically neutral and reversing it would reintroduce the exact duplication hazard being fixed.

When verifying a deploy-time defect (e.g. duplicated content in a regenerated file) is actually fixed, capturing the CURRENT live artifact before the fix is not sufficient evidence if the artifact self-heals on regeneration (a full-overwrite computed artifact can look clean between runs even with the bug present). Instead, capture a baseline immediately before the verification deploy runs, run the fixed code path, and diff/inspect the result -- and separately confirm the pre-fix live state still reproduced the defect at the start of verification (e.g. by inspecting a settings.json left over from a prior redeploy that ran before the code fix landed) as independent evidence the test would have caught the bug had the fix not been applied.
